title: Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1) (P0010-v2)
shortDescription: Bank 1 intake camshaft position actuator circuit fault. Stored as P0010-v2.
fullDescription: The PCM stores P0010-v2 when the camshaft variable timing system does not respond as commanded — either because the oil control valve cannot reach commanded duty cycle or the camshaft position diverges from the target. Bank 1 intake camshaft position actuator circuit fault. Oil quality and timing-chain wear dominate the failure mode.
safetyImpact: Driveable short-term; long-term operation can damage timing components.

causes.cause: Stuck or sludged oil control valve (OCV)
Wiring or connector fault on the OCV

fixSteps.title: Verify Oil Service
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm correct oil viscosity and recent service; top up as needed.

fixSteps.title: Test OCV
fixSteps.instruction: Bi-directional command the oil control valve and watch cam timing on scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Clean or Replace OCV
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the OCV and inspect the screen for sludge; replace if stuck.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Phaser & Chain
fixSteps.instruction: If OCV and oil are good, inspect timing chain stretch and cam phaser bolts.

faq.a: Brief drives are fine; prolonged driving with VVT faults can damage the chain or phasers.
Often yes — sludge in the OCV screen is a common cause and a flush + filter resolves many cases.

shortDescription: Coolant flow lower than expected — possible blocked passage or pump. Stored as P00B0-v2.
fullDescription: The PCM stores P00B0-v2 when measured coolant flow or warm-up rate is below expectation. Coolant flow lower than expected — possible blocked passage or pump. Most cases are stuck thermostats or trapped air, not pump failures.
safetyImpact: Watch temperature gauge; shut down if engine overheats.

fixSteps.title: Check Coolant Level
fixSteps.instruction: Top up to mark with the correct coolant type.

fixSteps.title: Bleed Air
fixSteps.instruction: Run the manufacturer bleed procedure with heater on full.

fixSteps.title: Test Thermostat
fixSteps.instruction: Compare upper and lower hose temperatures during warm-up.

fixSteps.title: Replace Thermostat or Pump
fixSteps.instruction: Install new thermostat / pump and refill with proper coolant.

faq.a: Watch the temp gauge; pull over and shut down if it climbs past normal.
Yes — mixing OAT and IAT chemistries can gel and block flow.

title: Fuel Level Output Circuit (P0656-v2)
shortDescription: Fuel level output circuit from PCM to gauge cluster fault. Stored as P0656-v2.
fullDescription: The PCM stores P0656-v2 for a fault in the fuel storage, supply, or measurement subsystem. Fuel level output circuit from PCM to gauge cluster fault. Verify with a pressure test before replacing parts.
safetyImpact: Stop driving if fuel smell or visible leak — fire risk.

causes.cause: Loose fuel cap or EVAP source for tank pressure faults

fixSteps.title: Visual Leak Check
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect lines, fittings, and rail for wet spots or fuel staining.

fixSteps.title: Pressure Test
fixSteps.instruction: Connect a fuel pressure gauge or read rail pressure on scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor or Sender
fixSteps.instruction: Verify sensor reads correctly across full range.

fixSteps.title: Repair Component
fixSteps.instruction: Replace failed pump, line, sender, or injector seal; clear codes.

faq.a: Stop driving if you smell fuel or see leaks — fire risk is real.
Not while a fuel-system code is active.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low (Bank 1) (P0661-v3)
shortDescription: Bank 1 intake manifold tuning valve control circuit shorted low. Stored as P0661-v3.
fullDescription: The PCM stores P0661-v3 when the intake manifold tuning valve or runner control does not move as commanded. Bank 1 intake manifold tuning valve control circuit shorted low. Carbon buildup on the flap shaft is the dominant cause on high-mileage engines.
safetyImpact: No safety risk; performance loss only.

causes.cause: Stuck IMTC valve from carbon buildup

fixSteps.title: Inspect Linkage
fixSteps.instruction: With engine off, manually verify manifold tuning flap moves freely.

fixSteps.title: Activate via Scan Tool
fixSteps.instruction: Bi-directional command the IMTC and watch for movement.

fixSteps.title: Test Solenoid Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Measure solenoid resistance and reference voltage at the connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace Component
fixSteps.instruction: Install new solenoid or actuator; clean carbon if linkage stuck.

faq.a: Yes for emissions, but with reduced low-RPM torque until fixed.
No — driveable, mainly a performance and code-clearing concern.
